reviewNotes: Rebuilt on 2026-10-17 with profile ci (opt-level 3, LTO disabled, codegen-units 16; not a fat-LTO release validation) in the pinned official rust:1.99.0-trixie image (index SHA-256 81015672d6939b0265f09adf96d5de125482bb1330106076956b0518e74edc90) with Debian 13 packages from snapshot 20261016T180000Z. dpkg evidence confirms gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64-win32 14.2.0-19+27+b1 (win32 thread model) and mingw-w64-x86-64-dev 12.0.0-5. The linker map links crt2.o, crtbegin.o/crtend.o, libmingw32/libmingwex runtime members, system import stubs, libgcc _ctors.o and libgcc_eh unwind-seh.o, now from the GCC 14 directory; no winpthreads member is present, and the fourteen reviewed native paths and eleven system DLL imports are otherwise unchanged from the Bookworm review. The Rust 1.99.0 standard-library aggregate and its twelve standalone sysroot texts are unchanged; preserve that complete aggregate and every notice/exception; compiler implementation dependencies remain outside the inventory. Reviewed the changed Debian copyright files verbatim: mingw-w64 12.0.0's adds header and IDL stanzas (LGPL-2.1+, expat, NCSA-LLVM) and reorganizes file lists, while the linked CRT and runtime objects keep their ZPL-2.1 and public-domain terms; gcc-mingw-w64's differs only in its packaging copyright year; GPL-3 is identical. libbcrypt.a is now SHA-256 db754b1ec02453061ba6e9fac313f07e30f43c128803c864ccfde255c731bd58; BCryptGenRandom remains an import trampoline to bcrypt.dll, covered by the mingw-w64 ZPL-2.1 attribution. The SystemFunction036 fallback uses ADVAPI32.dll. Retain the mingw-w64 copyright/ZPL-2.1 terms and disclaimer, and the GCC GPLv3 notices with GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1 for linked libgcc objects. Windows system DLLs are not bundled. Distributed builds check the native/import closure against this allowlist and check the actual notice text fingerprint. Binary hashes and full compiler version strings are not legal approval inputs; the pinned builder and toolchain establish their provenance. Rust 1.99.1, reviewed 2026-10-18 in the pinned rust:1.99.1-trixie builder (index SHA-256 e259494b14672950a909b4c54527e19d29cae6ebf980672114c8bb85e5594e4a): the point release changes only x86_64 argument-passing codegen and compiler-builtins' memory routines; its standard-library aggregate and twelve standalone sysroot texts are byte-identical to 1.99.0's, src/llvm-project stays at 1b9c0d5ff9bbe7634aead059efe6b11a7eeba145 and src/ci/docker/scripts/musl.sh is unchanged, so the reviewed native inputs, system imports, notice sources and fingerprint carry over.

reviewNotes: Built on 2026-10-18 with profile ci (opt-level 3, LTO disabled, codegen-units 16) and profile release (fat LTO, codegen-units 1, no PGO) in the pinned official rust:1.99.0-trixie image (index SHA-256 81015672d6939b0265f09adf96d5de125482bb1330106076956b0518e74edc90) with llvm-mingw 20261006 (llvm-mingw-20261006-ucrt-ubuntu-22.04-x86_64.tar.xz, SHA-256 5f9c6ed95b2d4bdb2869a488c5fd5857fbdabcf288a0aa3eb1da43f6a08d8ab4; LLVM 23.1 with the mingw-w64 UCRT runtime) unpacked at /opt/llvm-mingw. The collector links with -Ctarget-feature=+crt-static, so LLVM libunwind links statically instead of importing libunwind.dll. LLD's COFF map names archive members without their archive, so the build check sees only the startup objects crt2.o, crtbegin.o and crtend.o; the archives were reviewed from LLD's verbose load trace and its MSVC-style map: libmingw32.a, libmingwex.a and libmsvcrt.a (the UCRT variant's CRT glue and api-ms-win-crt import stubs), libunwind.a, and the import libraries libkernel32.a, libuser32.a, libntdll.a and libadvapi32.a. compiler-rt's libclang_rt.builtins-aarch64.a is searched but contributes no member, Rust's compiler_builtins providing those symbols, and no winpthreads or libc++ member links. The other system DLL imports come from windows-link raw-dylib and the reviewed windows_aarch64_gnullvm import library. Reviewed the shipped texts verbatim: mingw-w64's COPYING.MinGW-w64-runtime.txt (the runtime's ZPL-2.1 terms and disclaimer, with the ISC, BSD, gdtoa and public-domain parts it lists; its LGPL section covers headers and IDLs imported from Wine, which are not linked) and the LLVM project's LICENSE.TXT (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception and the legacy NCSA text) for libunwind. Retain both texts. The UCRT and the Windows system DLLs are part of Windows and not bundled. The Rust 1.99.0 standard-library aggregate and its twelve standalone sysroot texts are unchanged. Binary hashes and full compiler version strings are not legal approval inputs; the pinned builder, toolchain and llvm-mingw archive establish their provenance. Rust 1.99.1, reviewed 2026-10-18 in the pinned rust:1.99.1-trixie builder (index SHA-256 e259494b14672950a909b4c54527e19d29cae6ebf980672114c8bb85e5594e4a): the point release changes only x86_64 argument-passing codegen and compiler-builtins' memory routines; its standard-library aggregate and twelve standalone sysroot texts are byte-identical to 1.99.0's, src/llvm-project stays at 1b9c0d5ff9bbe7634aead059efe6b11a7eeba145 and src/ci/docker/scripts/musl.sh is unchanged, so the reviewed native inputs, system imports, notice sources and fingerprint carry over.

reviewNotes: Hosted CI run 37112635227 at commit 1a68553b generated the actual native linker maps and canonical input listings using the pinned official rust:1.99.0-bookworm image (index SHA-256 59037199c44290f2befcdd58dcc540164763fc296950255aaefeef096a1866b0). The probe used profile ci: opt-level 3, LTO disabled, codegen-units 16; it was not a fat-LTO release validation. The historical complete input listings match their original candidate fingerprints. The notice-only fingerprint was derived from those verified listings and retains every actual standard-library and additional notice text; the exported standard-library bytes were rechecked against their listed hashes. Reviewed the complete Rust 1.99.0 standard-library aggregate and all twelve standalone sysroot license texts. The standalone texts, in-tree notices and retained component notice bodies are unchanged from 1.98.1; dependency versions changed without new license expressions, and libc author metadata changed in the upstream aggregate. Preserve that complete aggregate and every notice/exception; compiler implementation dependencies remain outside the inventory. The x86_64 server and TUI canonical listings and actual native path sets are identical. Their maps link rcrt1.o, crti.o/crtn.o, crtbeginS.o/crtendS.o, libc.a and libunwind.a, with no imported system library; no GCC startup/runtime object is linked from the Debian driver. Rust 1.99.0 src/ci/docker/scripts/musl.sh pins musl 1.2.5 with the CVE-2025-26519, CVE-2026-6042 and CVE-2026-40200 patches; hosted native .comment evidence reports GCC 9.4.0. LLVM libunwind and compiler-rt startup source provenance is Rust 1.99.0's src/llvm-project submodule 1b9c0d5ff9bbe7634aead059efe6b11a7eeba145. Its exact libunwind/compiler-rt LICENSE.TXT bytes were inspected and remain identical to the existing Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception notices; rust-notice-sources.json pins their new source commit and unchanged hashes, together with the musl MIT copyright. Preserve all these notices. The probe observed the startup selection after Rust 1.99's static-PIE support change; distributed builds validate their native/import closure and notice text fingerprint. Binary hashes and full compiler version strings are not legal approval inputs; the pinned builder and toolchain establish their provenance. External musl/LLVM notice sources are bound to the pinned Rust version in rust-notice-sources.json, so toolchain upgrades require their source review even when paths and legal text bytes stay unchanged. Rebuilt on 2026-10-17 with profile ci in the pinned rust:1.99.0-trixie builder (index SHA-256 81015672d6939b0265f09adf96d5de125482bb1330106076956b0518e74edc90, Debian 13 snapshot 20261016T180000Z): the linked native paths, the absence of imported system libraries and the notice fingerprint are unchanged; C dependencies compiled with the Debian 13 cross compilers and musl 1.2.5-3.1~deb13u1 headers add Debian GCC 14.2.0 .comment evidence only. Rust 1.99.1, reviewed 2026-10-18 in the pinned rust:1.99.1-trixie builder (index SHA-256 e259494b14672950a909b4c54527e19d29cae6ebf980672114c8bb85e5594e4a): the point release changes only x86_64 argument-passing codegen and compiler-builtins' memory routines; its standard-library aggregate and twelve standalone sysroot texts are byte-identical to 1.99.0's, src/llvm-project stays at 1b9c0d5ff9bbe7634aead059efe6b11a7eeba145 and src/ci/docker/scripts/musl.sh is unchanged, so the reviewed native inputs, system imports, notice sources and fingerprint carry over.
